direction_as_read: mixed: some cognition and vascular signals from food-amount freeze-dried fruit, extract evidence thin, and several null results
summary: The labels sell extract, concentrate or powder at 100-800 mg per row. The stored review and most trials used freeze-dried fruit in food amounts, 20-26 g/day in the two trials that state it (36972800, 42251891). That evidence is itself mixed: one trial improved vascular and memory measures (36972800), and another found nothing on its primary biomarkers or on cognitive tests (42251891). Pooled results help episodic memory (40856863) but not most other tasks, or mood (35676847), and cardiovascular risk factors show insufficient evidence (33066847). Two extract trials come close to the labels, using one 100 mg proprietary purified extract for months (29882843) and single doses (38674870); effects were subtle, on few outcomes. No label row shows anthocyanin content, so label exposure can't be matched to the studied extract.
question_for_clinician: Do a proprietary 100 mg extract trial with a 3-month memory result (29882843) and acute extract studies (38674870) qualify unstandardized extract at 100-800 mg per row? Agent recommendation: no credit.
